data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Majeed" has been used throughout history in the Islamic world as a name that signifies greatness, power, and majesty. It is a name that is often given to those who are held in high esteem in their communities, and it conveys a sense of admiration and respect. In Arabic culture, the name "Majeed" is associated with noble qualities such as generosity, courage, and wisdom. People with this name may be seen as leaders, influencers, and role models.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic spirituality, the name "Majeed" has a deep spiritual significance. It is a reminder of the greatness and majesty of Allah, the one and only God. The name acknowledges the ultimate power and sovereignty of Allah, and it is a call to recognize and submit to His will. In Islamic teaching, "Majeed" is also associated with the concept of tawheed, or the oneness of God. It is a reminder to focus on the unity of God and to avoid associating any partners or equals with Him. Overall, the name "Majeed" is a powerful reminder of the infinite greatness and majesty of Allah, and it is a call to strive for righteousness and submission to His will.

historical_references.context: Majid ibn Harith was an Arab nobleman from the tribe of Kinda. He embraced Islam during the early years of the religion and became a close companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He participated in several battles and was known for his bravery and generosity. He is mentioned in several hadiths and is considered a significant figure in early Islamic history.
